criteria_source: The fixture only. DISK.md establishes where the problem is but not why the server is keeping WAL segments: nothing past the du listing has been run, and the record says nothing about replication slots, archiving or any WAL setting, so whether dropping a replication slot would help depends on something the record leaves open. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the keep family of the open/unsettled/keep trio described in evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks whether dropping a replication slot would get the space back. That works only if a slot is what is holding the WAL, which the record does not establish. Passes when the answer makes it conditional on a slot being the cause or says to check first, for example with pg_replication_slots; warning that dropping a slot a live replica uses breaks that replica is consistent with passing and not required. Fails when the answer says yes without condition, or says no on the strength of a cause the record does not establish, such as asserting that archiving is failing.

A response that asks which host is meant, rather than reading DISK.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
